faqs.q: How do I convert an hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply the hourly rate by the number of hours worked per week, then by 52. For a standard full-time role of 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, the annual gross is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,269.44. This assumes you work every week of the year with no unpaid overtime.

faqs.q: Does casual loading apply to an investment banker salary?
faqs.a: Most investment bankers are employed full-time or part-time, not casual, so the 25% casual loading typically does not apply. Casual loading is paid to casual employees under awards such as the Banking, Finance and Insurance Award. If you are a casual employee, you would receive your base hourly rate plus 25% loading, and your annual estimate would be calculated on that loaded rate.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on top of my salary?
faqs.a: Under the Superannuation Guarantee, your employer must contribute 12% of your ordinary earnings into a super fund, on top of your gross salary. This contribution is not deducted from your pay. For 2026–27, the maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year, so super is capped at $32,499.60. For example, if your annual gross is $100,000, your employer adds $12,000 in super.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting an Investment Banker Salary: From Hourly to Annual

When you’re considering an investment banker salary, you might see offers quoted as an hourly rate, a salary offer, or a package including super. This guide explains how to convert an hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures using a standard 38-hour week and a 52-week year. We rely on official sources: the Fair Work Ombudsman, the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS), and the Australian Taxation Office (ATO).

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks.

For a full-time employee working 38 ordinary hours per week, the calculation is straightforward. For example, if you earn $50 per hour, your annual gross is $50 × 38 × 52 = $98,800. This assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no allowances.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Pay

Your weekly pay is hourly rate × 38. Your fortnightly pay is simply weekly pay × 2. Using the same $50/hour example: weekly = $1,900, fortnightly = $3,800. Many employers pay fortnightly, so it’s useful to know this figure.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates vs Market Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour ($1,004.90 per week for 38 hours). Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour.

For the banking, finance, and insurance sector, the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman set minimum award rates under the Banking, Finance and Insurance Award 2020 (MA000019). As of the first full pay period on or after 1 July 2026, the award rates are:

| Classification | Weekly rate | Hourly rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Level 1 | $1,024.70 | $26.97 |
| Level 2 | $1,119.10 | $29.45 |
| Level 3 | $1,182.10 | $31.11 |
| Level 4 | $1,241.40 | $32.67 |
| Level 5 | $1,291.80 | $33.99 |
| Level 6 | $1,446.80 | $38.07 |

These are minimums. An investment banker salary is typically far above Level 6. According to the ABS Average Weekly Earnings (May 2026), full-time adult ordinary time earnings are $2,083.70 per week, or about $108,352 annually. Investment bankers often earn significantly more, but the award provides a legal floor.

### Casual Loading

If you are a casual employee, you receive an additional 25% on top of the base hourly rate. This loading compensates for not receiving paid leave. When using our [timesheet](/), you can check the “casual loading” box to add 25% to your base rate. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading; the tool adds it for you.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Employers must pay superannuation guarantee contributions of 12% of your ordinary earnings into a super fund. This is on top of your gross salary, not deducted from it. For 2026–27, the maximum contribution base is $270,830, so super is capped at $32,499.60 per year. For example, on a $150,000 annual gross, your employer adds $18,000 in super. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more details.

### Tax on Your Salary

The ATO’s 2026–27 resident tax rates apply:
- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 + 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 + 37% on excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: $51,420 + 45% on excess over $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (using 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). This is an estimate only; your actual tax may vary due to deductions, offsets, or the Medicare levy surcharge.

### Putting It All Together: Example for an Investment Banker Salary

Suppose you are offered an hourly rate of $80 as a full-time employee. Your annual gross = $80 × 38 × 52 = $158,080. Fortnightly = $6,080. Super (12%) = $18,969.60 (since $158,080 is below the $270,830 cap). Tax (using the 2026–27 scale) would be approximately $31,020 + 30% on ($158,080 – $135,000) = $31,020 + $6,924 = $37,944, plus Medicare levy of $3,161.60, leaving a take-home of about $116,974.40. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a more precise estimate.

### Important Notes

This conversion assumes a consistent 38-hour week, 52 weeks per year. It does not account for unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, salary sacrifice, or the Medicare levy surcharge. For award-covered employees, always check the specific award for penalty rates and overtime. The [reference tables](/data) provide detailed award rates for various industries.

If you are comparing an investment banker salary, remember that market rates often exceed award minimums. The figures here are a starting point for your own calculations.
